title: Moving Charges and Magnetism
syllabus: Biot-Savart law and its application to current carrying circular loop; Ampere's law and its applications to infinitely long straight wire and solenoid; Force on a moving charge in uniform magnetic and electric fields (Lorentz force); Motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field; Cyclotron; Force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field, force between two parallel current-carrying conductors-definition of ampere; Torque experienced by a current loop in uniform magnetic field; Moving coil galvanometer-its current sensitivity and conversion to ammeter and voltmeter

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A charged particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ is moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ in a region of uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ perpendicular to $\vec{v}$. The time period of its circular revolution is independent of:
questions.solution:
Centripetal force is provided by the magnetic Lorentz force:
$$\frac{m v^2}{R} = q v B \implies R = \frac{m v}{q B}$$
Time period of revolution:
$$T = \frac{2\pi R}{v} = \frac{2\pi}{v} \left(\frac{m v}{q B}\right) = \frac{2\pi m}{q B}$$
Hence, $T$ depends only on mass, charge, and magnetic field, and is independent of speed $v$ and radius $R$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A circular coil of wire consisting of 100 turns, each of radius $8.0\text{ cm}$, carries a current of $0.40\text{ A}$. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil is (take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}$):
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of $N$ turns:
$$B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R}$$
Substitute $N = 100$, $I = 0.40\text{ A}$, $R = 0.08\text{ m}$:
$$B = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times 100 \times 0.40}{2 \times 0.08} = \frac{1.6\pi \times 10^{-5}}{0.16} = \pi \times 10^{-4}\text{ T}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An electron and a proton having the same kinetic energy enter perpendicularly into a uniform magnetic field. If $r_e$ and $r_p$ are their respective orbital radii, then the ratio $\frac{r_e}{r_p}$ is:
questions.solution:
Radius of circular path in a magnetic field is $r = \frac{p}{q B} = \frac{\sqrt{2m K}}{q B}$.
Since both have identical charge magnitude $e$, kinetic energy $K$, and magnetic field $B$:
$$r \propto \sqrt{m}$$
$$\frac{r_e}{r_p} = \sqrt{\frac{m_e}{m_p}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A long straight wire of radius $a$ carries a steady current $I$ uniformly distributed over its cross-section. The ratio of the magnetic field at distance $a/2$ from the wire axis to that at distance $2a$ from the axis is:
questions.solution:
Inside the wire ($r_1 = a/2 < a$):
$$B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I r_1}{2\pi a^2} = \frac{\mu_0 I (a/2)}{2\pi a^2} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}$$
Outside the wire ($r_2 = 2a > a$):
$$B_2 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r_2} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi (2a)} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}$$
$$\frac{B_1}{B_2} = \frac{\mu_0 I / 4\pi a}{\mu_0 I / 4\pi a} = 1 : 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Two parallel long straight conductors carrying currents $I_1$ and $I_2$ in the same direction separated by distance $d$ in vacuum exert an attractive force per unit length given by:
questions.solution:
Magnetic field produced by conductor 1 at the location of conductor 2 is $B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d}$.
Magnetic force on length $L$ of conductor 2 carrying current $I_2$:
$$F = I_2 L B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2 L}{2\pi d}$$
Force per unit length is attractive for currents in the same direction:
$$\frac{F}{L} = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A square loop of side $a$ carries a steady current $I$. The magnetic field at the centre of the square loop is:
questions.solution:
Distance from each straight segment to the centre is $d = a/2$.
Each segment subtends angles $\theta_1 = \theta_2 = 45^\circ$ at the centre.
Magnetic field due to one side:
$$B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi d}(\sin 45^\circ + \sin 45^\circ) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi (a/2)}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}\sqrt{2}$$
By right-hand rule, fields from all 4 sides point in the same direction:
$$B_{\text{total}} = 4 B_1 = 4 \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}\right) = \frac{2\sqrt{2}\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A moving coil galvanometer has $N$ turns, each of effective area $A$, suspended in a radial magnetic field $B$. If the torsional constant of the suspension fibre is $C$, its current sensitivity is given by:
questions.solution:
Deflecting torque in radial field: $\tau_{\text{def}} = N I A B$.
Restoring torque: $\tau_{\text{res}} = C \theta$.
In equilibrium: $C \theta = N I A B \implies \theta = \left(\frac{N A B}{C}\right) I$.
Current sensitivity is deflection per unit current:
$$S_i = \frac{\theta}{I} = \frac{N A B}{C}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle with charge $q$ moves with velocity $\vec{v} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\text{ m/s}$ in a combined electric and magnetic field $\vec{E} = 2\hat{k}\text{ V/m}$ and $\vec{B} = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j})\text{ T}$. The Lorentz force acting on the particle is:
questions.solution:
Lorentz force is $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v} \times \vec{B})$:
$$\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{k}(3 \times 3 - 4 \times 2) = \hat{k}(9 - 8) = 1\hat{k}$$
$$\vec{F} = q(2\hat{k} + 1\hat{k}) = q(3\hat{k})\text{ N}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A tightly wound long solenoid of length $L$ and radius $r$ ($L \gg r$) has $n$ turns per unit length and carries a steady current $I$. The magnetic field near the edge at an axial end of the solenoid is:
questions.solution:
For an infinitely long solenoid, the axial magnetic field near the middle is $B = \mu_0 n I$.
At either end face of a semi-infinite solenoid, half of the symmetrical turn distribution is absent, so the axial magnetic field is:
$$B_{\text{end}} = \frac{1}{2}\mu_0 n I$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A circular loop of radius $R$ carrying a current $I$ produces magnetic field $B_0$ at its centre. The distance along its axis from the centre where the magnetic field becomes $\frac{B_0}{8}$ is:
questions.solution:
Axial field of a circular loop: $B(x) = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$.
At the centre ($x = 0$): $B_0 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.
$$B(x) = B_0 \left( \frac{R^3}{(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}} \right) = \frac{B_0}{8}$$
$$\frac{R^3}{(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}} = \frac{1}{8} \implies \frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + x^2}} = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\sqrt{R^2 + x^2} = 2R \implies R^2 + x^2 = 4R^2 \implies x^2 = 3R^2 \implies x = \sqrt{3} R$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] In a velocity selector, mutually perpendicular electric field $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ act on a beam of charged particles. The particles pass undeflected through the selector if their speed equals:
questions.solution:
For undeflected transmission, the electric force balances the magnetic force:
$$q E = q v B \implies v = \frac{E}{B}$$

questions.question: A charged particle moves in a uniform magnetic field. Which of the following quantities associated with the particle remains strictly constant during its motion?
questions.solution:
The magnetic Lorentz force is always perpendicular to velocity: $\vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \cdot \vec{v} = 0$.
Since instantaneous power is zero, no work is done on the particle, and its speed and kinetic energy remain constant.
The direction of velocity, momentum, and acceleration continuously change.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A wire of length $L$ carrying current $I$ is bent into a circular loop of $n$ turns. The magnetic dipole moment of the loop is proportional to:
questions.solution:
Length of wire: $L = n(2\pi r) \implies r = \frac{L}{2\pi n}$.
Area of each turn: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \left(\frac{L}{2\pi n}\right)^2 = \frac{L^2}{4\pi n^2}$.
Magnetic moment of the coil:
$$M = n I A = n I \left(\frac{L^2}{4\pi n^2}\right) = \frac{I L^2}{4\pi n} \propto \frac{1}{n}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A straight wire carrying current $I$ is placed in a uniform magnetic field $B$. The force acting on a segment of length $L$ of the wire is zero when:
options: The wire is parallel or antiparallel to $\vec{B}$
The wire makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with $\vec{B}$
The magnetic field is non-zero and non-uniform
questions.solution:
The magnetic force on a current-carrying wire is $\vec{F} = I(\vec{L} \times \vec{B})$.
Magnitude: $F = I L B \sin\theta$.
When the wire is parallel ($\theta = 0^\circ$) or antiparallel ($\theta = 180^\circ$) to the magnetic field, $\sin\theta = 0$, giving $F = 0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An electron moves in a circular orbit of radius $r$ with angular speed $\omega$ around a nucleus. The equivalent magnetic dipole moment of the revolving electron is:
questions.solution:
Orbital period of electron: $T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}$.
Equivalent electric current: $I = \frac{e}{T} = \frac{e\omega}{2\pi}$.
Area enclosed by orbit: $A = \pi r^2$.
Magnetic dipole moment:
$$\mu = I A = \left(\frac{e\omega}{2\pi}\right)(\pi r^2) = \frac{1}{2} e \omega r^2$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A helical motion of a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ occurs when the initial velocity $\vec{v}$ makes an arbitrary angle $\theta$ ($0 < \theta < 90^\circ$) with $\vec{B}$. The pitch of the helix is:
questions.solution:
Velocity parallel to the magnetic field: $v_\parallel = v\cos\theta$.
Time period of circular motion in the transverse plane: $T = \frac{2\pi m}{q B}$.
Pitch $p$ is the linear distance traversed along $\vec{B}$ in one full revolution:
$$p = v_\parallel T = (v\cos\theta)\left(\frac{2\pi m}{q B}\right) = \frac{2\pi m v \cos\theta}{q B}$$

questions.question: A planar current loop of arbitrary shape carrying current $I$ is placed in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$. The net magnetic force acting on the complete closed loop is:
questions.solution:
Net magnetic force on a closed circuit in a uniform field is:
$$\vec{F} = \oint I (d\vec{l} \times \vec{B}) = I \left(\oint d\vec{l}\right) \times \vec{B}$$
For any closed loop, the vector sum of displacement around the loop is zero: $\oint d\vec{l} = 0$.
Therefore, $\vec{F} = 0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A proton and an alpha particle enter a uniform magnetic field with the same momentum perpendicular to the field. The ratio of the radii of their circular paths $\frac{r_p}{r_\alpha}$ is:
questions.solution:
Radius of circular path: $r = \frac{p}{q B}$.
Both particles have identical momentum $p$ and move in the same magnetic field $B$:
$$r \propto \frac{1}{q}$$
$$\frac{r_p}{r_\alpha} = \frac{q_\alpha}{q_p} = \frac{2e}{e} = 2 : 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A toroid of mean radius $20\text{ cm}$ has 500 turns and carries a current of $2.0\text{ A}$. The magnetic field inside the core of the toroid is (take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}$):
questions.solution:
Magnetic field in a toroid of mean radius $R$ and $N$ turns:
$$B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2\pi R}$$
Substitute $N = 500$, $I = 2.0\text{ A}$, $R = 0.20\text{ m}$:
$$B = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times 500 \times 2.0}{2\pi \times 0.20} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 1000}{0.20} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-4}}{0.20} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ T}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Ampere's circuital law states that the line integral of magnetic field $\vec{B}$ around a closed path equals:
questions.solution:
Ampere's circuital law in integral form for steady currents states:
$$\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_{\text{enc}}$$
where $I_{\text{enc}}$ is the total conduction current passing through any open surface bounded by the closed Amperian loop.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A straight horizontal wire of mass $0.1\text{ kg}$ and length $0.5\text{ m}$ carries a current of $2.0\text{ A}$. Find the minimum magnitude of magnetic field (in Tesla) required to suspend the wire in air against gravity (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$).
questions.solution:
For magnetic levitation against gravity, the upward magnetic force balances weight:
$$F_m = I L B = m g$$
$$B = \frac{m g}{I L} = \frac{0.1 \times 10}{2.0 \times 0.5} = \frac{1.0}{1.0} = 1.0\text{ T}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A proton is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of $1000\text{ V}$ and then enters perpendicularly into a uniform magnetic field of $0.1\text{ T}$. Find the radius (in cm) of its circular path (take $m_p = 1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$ and $q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, rounded to one decimal place).
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy acquired: $K = q V = (1.6 \times 10^{-19})(1000) = 1.6 \times 10^{-16}\text{ J}$.
Momentum:
$$p = \sqrt{2m K} = \sqrt{2(1.67 \times 10^{-27})(1.6 \times 10^{-16})} = \sqrt{5.344 \times 10^{-43}} = \sqrt{53.44} \times 10^{-22} \approx 7.31 \times 10^{-22}\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$$
Radius:
$$R = \frac{p}{q B} = \frac{7.31 \times 10^{-22}}{(1.6 \times 10^{-19})(0.1)} = \frac{7.31 \times 10^{-22}}{1.6 \times 10^{-20}} = 4.568 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m} = 4.57\text{ cm} \approx 4.6\text{ cm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A rectangular coil of dimensions $10\text{ cm} \times 5\text{ cm}$ having 50 turns carries a current of $2.0\text{ A}$. The coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field of $0.2\text{ T}$ such that the plane of the coil makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the field direction. Find the torque (in $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$) acting on the coil (rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Area of the coil: $A = 0.10 \times 0.05 = 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^2$.
Magnetic moment:
$$M = N I A = 50 \times 2.0 \times (5.0 \times 10^{-3}) = 0.50\text{ A}\cdot\text{m}^2$$
The normal to the coil's plane makes an angle $\theta = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$ with $\vec{B}$.
Torque:
$$\tau = M B \sin\theta = 0.50 \times 0.2 \times \sin 60^\circ = 0.10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 0.05 \times 1.732 \approx 0.0866\text{ N}\cdot\text{m} \approx 0.09\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An infinitely long straight conductor carries a current of $50\text{ A}$. Find the magnitude of magnetic field (in $\mu\text{T}$) at a perpendicular distance of $10\text{ cm}$ from the conductor.
questions.solution:
Magnetic field due to an infinitely long straight wire:
$$B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d}$$
Substitute $I = 50\text{ A}$ and $d = 0.1\text{ m}$:
$$B = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times 50}{2\pi \times 0.1} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 50}{0.1} = \frac{10^{-5}}{0.1} = 10^{-4}\text{ T} = 100.0\,\mu\text{T}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Two long parallel wires are separated by $5\text{ cm}$ and carry currents $I_1 = 10\text{ A}$ and $I_2 = 20\text{ A}$ in opposite directions. Find the force per unit length (in $\text{N/m}$) exerted on each wire in units of $10^{-4}\text{ N/m}$ (take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}$).
questions.solution:
Force per unit length between two parallel conductors:
$$\frac{F}{L} = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$$
Substitute $I_1 = 10\text{ A}$, $I_2 = 20\text{ A}$, and $d = 0.05\text{ m}$:
$$\frac{F}{L} = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times 10 \times 20}{2\pi \times 0.05} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 200}{0.05} = \frac{4 \times 10^{-5}}{0.05} = 8.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ N/m}$$
Value in units of $10^{-4}\text{ N/m}$ is $8.0$.
